_provenance.purpose: Real BNR/CRB codification tables, extracted and preserved so lib/crb-report.ts (and any future BNR/CRB work) can cite real codes instead of leaving fields blank or guessing. Built 2026-08-23 during a full read-through of all three official source documents.

sources.title: TransUnion Rwanda Data Specification Document, Version 1.9 (01/01/2018)
sources.note: Official CRB data-submission spec. Confirms Classification labels/order (page 14, Consumer; page 24, Corporate) and the full Nature/Category code tables (pages 17-19, 27-29). Does not itself list Classification day-boundaries or the Sector of Activity code table.

sources.title: Codification BNR 29 april 2010
sources.note: Older BNR reference workbook. Sheets: CREDIT NATURES, Credit Category, ACTIVITY SECTORS, CLASSES, payment frequencies. Read directly by Kevin; cross-checked against the other two sources rather than re-extracted by script.

sources.title: BNR CODIFICATION New template.xls
sources.preservedAt: Supabase Storage, bucket 'reference-documents', path 'bnr-codification/bnr-codification-new-template.xls' (NOT committed to git — 2.9MB binary; see docs/known-gaps.md entry dated 2026-08-23 for why)
sources.note: Newest, most complete reference workbook. Sheets used here: CLASSIFICATION, occupation, legal status, loan Category, sector of activity, consu revised (the real Consumer field spec — confirms Occupation and Sector of Activity both say 'consider the list provided', i.e. these sheets are the intended code source).

classification.description: BNR/CRB loan classification by days in arrears. Used live by lib/calculator.ts classifyByDays() (CRB generator, BNR generator from Item E2, admin UI).
classification.status: USED — boundaries realigned 2026-09-10 to REGULATION No 65/04/2023 Article 39(1). Kevin's deliberate decision as business owner (Item E1): the regulation's 'at least one day' for Watch supersedes the 0-29 day 'Normal grace window' previously carried from the bnr-template 'CLASSIFICATION' sheet / transunion-v1.9. Those two sources disagree with the binding regulation; the regulation wins. The 2026-08-23 'day-boundary fix' that had moved days 1-29 from Watch to Normal is hereby reversed.

codes.label: NORMAL RISK
codes.note: Art. 39(1)(a): current, no delay or unpaid instalment. 0% provision.

codes.label: WATCH
codes.note: Art. 39(1)(b): at least one instalment in arrears for at least ONE day. 1% provision.

codes.label: WRITE OFF
codes.note: Art. 41: >= 1 year in Loss class + board approval. Not derivable from days in arrears alone; never auto-assigned by classifyByDays().

classification.sourceNote: PRIMARY SOURCE as of 2026-09-10: 'Regulation No 65/04/2023 of 25/04/2023 governing non-deposit-taking financial service providers' (the binding BNR regulation; official BNR publication, not stored in this repo), Article 39(1): 'watch: loans or commitments with at least one or part of the instalment in arrears for at least one day.' Provision rates 0/1/20/50/100% from the same article; Art. 39(2) cross-default, Art. 41 write-off, Art. 42 documentation, Art. 45 collateral haircuts, Art. 47(c) restructured-loan classification also implemented (Items E3-E6). This supersedes the earlier day boundaries from bnr-template sheet 'CLASSIFICATION' (which had a 0-29 Normal window and a '90 - 189' Substandard typo). transunion-v1.9 (Consumer p.14 / Corporate p.24) is retained only as the label/ordering cross-reference (1=NORMAL RISK .. 6=WRITE OFF), not as the day-boundary authority.

nature.description: BNR 'Nature' of credit facility — French-language codes distinguishing account type/maturity structure (current-account vs. short/medium/long-term credit, signature credit, etc.).
nature.status: USED — see docs/known-gaps.md entry dated 2026-08-23 (second Nature/Category entry). lib/crb-report.ts natureCode() maps loan_type='Salary Advance' to code 13 (the one case specific enough for a non-catch-all code); every other loan_type falls through to the real catch-all, code 39 (AUTRES CREDITS A DECAISSEMENT).
nature.sourceNote: Confirmed identical between transunion-v1.9 (pages 17 and 27) and Kevin's read of bnr-codification-2010.

category.description: BNR 'Category' of credit facility — French-language codes for the purpose/product type of the loan.
category.status: USED — see docs/known-gaps.md entry dated 2026-08-23 (second Nature/Category entry). lib/crb-report.ts categoryCode() maps loan_type='Salary Advance' to code 40 (CREDITS PERSONNELS); every other loan_type falls through to the real catch-all, code 39 (AUTRES CREDITS A DECAISSEMENT — the same code and label as Nature's catch-all, confirmed identical in both tables).
category.sourceNote: Confirmed identical between transunion-v1.9 (pages 18 and 28) and bnr-template sheet 'loan Category'. bnr-template additionally uses the English label 'Personal Loan' for code 40 and 'Cash Advance' for code 10 — kept the French labels here since they're what both spec documents use verbatim.

sectorOfActivity.description: BNR 4-digit hierarchical economic sector classification (ECONOMIC_SECTOR_L1/L2/L3/SUB). Top-level (L1) codes shown here in full; the complete 4-level, 77-row hierarchy (finer sub-sectors, e.g. 1111=Agriculture For Coffee Exports) lives in the preserved source documents, not duplicated here.
sectorOfActivity.status: USED — see fix dated 2026-08-23 in docs/known-gaps.md. lib/crb-report.ts now maps iacm_loans.economic_sector text to one of these L1 codes instead of writing the raw English text into the CRB file.

inemaMapping.description: Confirmed 2026-08-23 mapping from INEMA's current iacm_loans.economic_sector free-text values to the real L1 code, used directly by lib/crb-report.ts.

sectorOfActivity.sourceNote: L1 table from bnr-template sheet 'sector of activity', confirmed matching the 'ACTIVITY SECTORS' table Kevin read in bnr-codification-2010. 'Health' maps to 9200 (L2 'Health And Related Services' under L1 9000), not the bare L1 9000, since it's specific enough to use the finer code. transunion-v1.9 lists this field as Text, max length 2 (pages 19, 29) — that's inconsistent with the real 4-digit codes in both codification sources and is almost certainly a copy-paste leftover from the adjacent Nature/Category rows (which genuinely are 2-digit); the 4-digit codes are used here since they're what both dedicated codification documents actually define.
